The Gemara cites a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says: When the Tabernacle was erected, the people were commanded to refrain from carrying out on Shabbat, as it is stated: “Each man shall remain in his place; no man shall go out of his place on the seventh day” (Exodus 16:29). Subsequently, when the Tabernacle was dismantled, they were commanded to refrain from carrying out, as it is stated: “They shall not go into the sacred place, lest they bear iniquity, and die” (Numbers 18:22). Just as the prohibition against carrying out stated when the Tabernacle was erected was a prohibition against carrying out from domain to domain, so too, the prohibition stated when it was dismantled was a prohibition against carrying out from domain to domain.

Abaye said to Rava: If that is so, then the prohibition against carrying out from domain to domain was stated at the time of the erection of the Tabernacle and was repeated at the time of its dismantling. If so, there are two verses that come as one, i.e., to teach one matter, and there is a principle that any two verses that come as one do not teach a halakha to apply to other cases. And if you say that the prohibition against carrying out from domain to domain was stated only at the time of the dismantling of the Tabernacle, and the prohibition stated at the time of the erection of the Tabernacle was in reference to the halakha of Shabbat boundaries, that is difficult.

This is as it is taught in a baraita that Ḥananya says: The prohibition against traveling beyond the Shabbat boundary is from Torah law, and the warning in the verse “Let no man go out of his place on the seventh day” is referring to the halakha of Shabbat boundaries. There is a difficulty with this, as we found that the prohibitions of carrying out and of Shabbat boundaries were each stated with regard to the Tabernacle. Therefore, that baraita contradicts our baraita. Rather, isn’t it correct to conclude from it that the prohibition against carrying out was stated at the time of the erection and at the time of the dismantling of the Tabernacle, and the prohibition against traveling beyond the Shabbat boundary was stated only at the time of the erection of the Tabernacle? The Gemara rejects this: No; actually, the prohibition against carrying out was stated at the time of the erection of the Tabernacle, and the prohibition against Shabbat boundaries was stated at the time of its dismantling. And this is what the baraita means to say: Just as the prohibition stated at the time of the erection of the Tabernacle was a prohibition against carrying out from domain to domain, so too, the prohibition stated at the time of its dismantling was a prohibition against carrying out from domain to domain.
